title: Proper and smooth functoriality of the deformation defect
statement:
Fix the algebraically closed field $k$ and finite coefficient ring $A=A_{E,n}$ of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Use the specialization datum of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] and the Rees deformation of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry]. Let $X,X'$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and write $z:Z\hookrightarrow N_{Z/X}$ for the zero section. For $M\in D^b_c(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes], put
$$C_{X,Z}(M)=\operatorname{cone}(z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\to i^*M),$$
using the canonical zero-section map, defined as follows. The closed immersion $i$ maps the pair $(Z,Z)$ to $(X,Z)$, so it has the lift $\widetilde i:Z_D\hookrightarrow\widetilde X_Z$ of [lem-trf-dnc-functorial-geometry], whose special fibre is $z$. The canonical zero-section map is the composite
$$z^*\operatorname{sp}_{\widetilde X_Z}M\xrightarrow{\mathrm{BC}^*}\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}i^*M\xrightarrow{\theta^{-1}}i^*M,$$
where $\mathrm{BC}^*$ is the base-change map of [def-trf-deformation-specialization] for $\widetilde i$ and $\theta:N\to\operatorname{sp}_{Z_D}N$ is the nearby-cycle unit of the constant lift $Z_D$. Part of the assertion is that $\theta$ is an isomorphism for every $N\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Let $h:X'\to X$ be a $k$-morphism, $Z'=h^{-1}Z$ scheme-theoretically, and $h_Z:Z'\to Z$ its restriction. If $h$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then for every $M'\in D^b_c(X'_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$C_{X,Z}(Rh_*M')\cong Rh_{Z*}C_{X',Z'}(M').$$
If $h$ is smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], then
$$C_{X',Z'}(h^*M)\cong h_Z^*C_{X,Z}(M).$$
These comparisons are natural in the complexes and compatible with composition, localization triangles, and restriction to open subsets. The defect construction is triangulated. For the complementary open immersion $j:X\setminus Z\hookrightarrow X$, the localization morphism $C_{X,Z}(j_!j^*M)\to C_{X,Z}(M)$ is an isomorphism. For every $N\in D^b_c(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ one has $C_{X,Z}(i_*N)=0$.
